what: The in-place-chain docs enumerate the safe input-pop/output-reserve lifecycle PAIRS and frame the whole hazard as CB self-DEADLOCK (no-hang + correct values). They never state the second requirement: an in-place chain ROTATES the CB front by the whole iteration window, so if a LATER stage reads that CB with a bulk cb_wait_front plus linear tile indexing, the ring must be sized for the rotation or the window straddles the wrap. Getting the lifecycle pair right and the ring size wrong gives SILENTLY WRONG VALUES on the partial final block only -- the worst failure class, and invisible whenever the block count divides evenly. I only got it right by recognising it as the seed D6 hazard on a different CB and doubling cb_normalized.
suggest: Add a third bullet to inplace_chain.cpp header (and the chain.hpp in-place note): in-place advances the CB front by the iteration window, so a downstream BULK reader of the same CB needs ring >= 2x the largest window; state that violating it is a wrong ANSWER, not a hang, unlike the lifecycle-pair hazard above it.

what: The design contradicts itself on cb_normalized. The CB table row says it is allocated only when !HAS_RESIDUAL because with a residual cb_x_sum plays this role too; the Key Risks row says the held cb_x_sum is written by residual_add_block and read by square/normalize, NEVER aliased. Both cannot hold: cb_x_sum is pass B srcA at Upfront/None with a tile base, which is exactly the operand shape an in-place chain forbids as its output, so following the CB table deadlocks. Cost was a design-authority judgement call in the middle of implementation, and a future agent reading the same table can implement the deadlocking version.
suggest: Design authoring: when a CB row proposes an in-place alias, cross-check it against the in-place operand-policy constraint and against the op design Key Risks table before shipping; here the CB-table row should be corrected to allocate cb_normalized under (HAS_GAMMA || HAS_BIAS) regardless of the residual.

what: Two golden-suite defects that are op-independent and silently delete coverage on this ttnn build. (1) sharded_config_for reads CoreRange.end_coord/.start_coord; this build exposes .start/.end, so the stand-in raises AttributeError BEFORE the op is called -- that removes the ENTIRE program_config loose group (7 cells) plus 3 of test_validation.py refusal tests, i.e. the whole config-consuming surface goes untested while looking like 10 op failures. (2) check_output -> compute_metrics_torch calls torch.max() on the readback, which raises on a 0-element tensor, so the 3 zero-volume loose cells fail AFTER the op returned a correct empty tensor (shape/dtype/layout all checked and passing first). Cost was real triage time deciding these were not mine, and the coverage loss is permanent for every future run of this op.
suggest: Fix program_config.py to bbox.start/.end (matching every other consumer in the tree, e.g. the seed descriptor), and give metrics.compute_metrics_torch an early return for numel()==0 that reports a trivially-passing metric set. Until then a future implementer should be told, in the golden-tests contract, that a traceback whose deepest frame is inside eval/ is harness-side.

what: The tt-probe.sh example shows a heredoc that imports torch+ttnn and then dots, with no device acquisition -- while the surrounding text is emphatic that tests must never create a device. First probe died on NameError: name device is not defined, and the safe fix (ttnn.open_device in a probe) reads like a violation of the adjacent rule until you notice the one clause that exempts probes. One wasted device run per agent that starts with a probe.
suggest: Make the tt-probe example self-contained: show device = ttnn.open_device(device_id=0) at the top and ttnn.close_device(device) at the bottom, with a one-line note that a probe is not a test file so this is the intended pattern here.
